Ben: Heads-up — noticed a regression in streaming token tail after yesterday's kernel scheduler change + adaptive-batching tweak. p95 token-latency went from ~28ms -> ~120ms on a handful of routes.
Leila: Ugh. Any perf profiles or a quick diff of the rollout? Was this the kernel-selection heuristic change (kernel-v2) or the batching window shrink? @Marcus any visibility from client traces?
Ben: I grabbed a short trace from route /chat/generate — here's the token timing summary (from our token-level telemetry):
```
route: /chat/generate
baseline (before): p50=14ms p95=28ms p99=65ms
after change:       p50=16ms p95=120ms p99=380ms
notes: tail shows repeated 40-60ms spikes every ~5 tokens
```
Marcus: I pulled a client vs server split — client ack time is stable. Server-side shows repeated kernel selection rebinds during a single sequence (kernel-hotswap). Looks like the runtime is flipping from fast-matmul -> quantized-path back to fast-matmul due to dynamic kernel scoring when seq_len grows. That churn can add ~30-50ms per token in the worst case.
Leila: OK that fits with what we saw in the profiler: small kernel-change hysteresis + aggressive batch-splitting caused a lot of micro-restarts. Also KV cache eviction rate spiked on those hosts (evictions/sec ~5x). Could be related: when kernel rebind happens we flush some per-thread caches.
Ben: Attaching snippet from host logs showing kernel rebind events and batching metric around the same timeframe:
```
[2026-03-15T18:02:01Z] kernel_switch: host=gpux-12 reason=heuristic_score_delta old=matmul_v1 new=quantized_v2
[2026-03-15T18:02:01Z] batch_window=8 -> 4 (adaptive) inflight=11
[2026-03-15T18:02:02Z] kv_cache_evict key_prefix=seq-123 evict_count=27
[2026-03-15T18:02:02Z] kernel_switch: host=gpux-12 reason=heuristic_score_delta old=quantized_v2 new=matmul_v1
```
Marcus: Proposed quick mitigation: 1) increase kernel hysteresis threshold so we don't flip mid-sequence, 2) don't shrink batching window below 6 tokens when sequential stream is flagged, 3) avoid flushing KV on kernel switch (or delay eviction until sequence end). Which should we push to canary?
Leila: I'd push #1 first (safe), then #3 as config toggle. #2 needs more thought — it affects latency for short requests. Can we do a canary for a single pool with the hysteresis bump? @SRE-Dana can you target gpux-12 pool for a 10% traffic canary?
SRE-Dana: deploy-bot will schedule the config bump now for pool gpux-12 at 10% traffic. I'll watch token-level p95 and KV eviction rates. +alert if p95 > 150ms for 5m.
deploy-bot: Configuration rollout started: kernel_hysteresis=+0.12, target_pools=[gpux-12], traffic=10% :rocket:
Ben: Thanks. If this drops the flip rate and stabilizes tail we'll proceed. Will gather a 30m rolling trace and post results here. :thumbsup:
